{{AnimeLocationInfobox |name=Crown City |characters=クラウンシティ |japanese=Crown City |image=Crown City.png |imagesize=300px |caption=Incoming view of Crown City |epicode=M13 |episode=Zoroark: Master of Illusions |region=Sinnoh |colorscheme=HGSS }} '''Crown City''' (Japanese: '''クラウンシティ''' ''Crown City'') is an {{pkmn|animated series}}-exclusive location in the [[Sinnoh]] [[region]] and the setting of ''[[M13|Zoroark: Master of Illusions]]''. ==History== Twenty years prior, a disaster caused all plant life in Crown City to die out. That was also the last time before the present that {{p|Celebi}} had appeared in the city. Fortunately, with the help of both humans and Pokémon working together, the city was brought back to its beautiful state. {{ash}} and {{ashfr}} visit the city to watch the [[Pokémon Baccer World Cup]]. Along the way, they meet a Pokémon named {{p|Zorua}} and decide to help it search for its "Meema." Meema is {{p|Zoroark}}, who has been blackmailed by businessman [[Grings Kodai]] into creating the illusion of the city's destruction in the forms of {{p|Raikou}}, {{p|Entei}} and {{p|Suicune}}. The {{OBP|Legendary beasts|M13}} are considered the city's protectors. In the film, {{Shiny}} versions of the trio had sensed the city was in danger while Zoroark was destroying it in illusions of its destruction, and raced to Crown City to defend it. After Zoroark broke free of her prison when she had been recaptured by Kodai, the legendary beasts appear before the Illusion Fox Pokémon and attacked her, believing her to be responsible for the city's destruction. When the misunderstanding is resolved thanks to the local wild Pokémon who live in the city, the legendary beasts aided Zoroark in the final battle against Kodai. Crown City made a brief reappearance in ''[[M20|I Choose You!]]'', which is set in a timeline different from the main series. ==Gallery== Crown City art.jpg|Aerial view Inside Crown City.jpg|Buildings in the city Crown City housing.png|Housing Crown City waterway.png|Waterway Crown City at Dawn.png|At dawn Baccer World Cup Stadium.png|The Pokémon Baccer World Cup stadium ==Trivia== * Crown City was used as the [[Original Trainer|OT]] of Japanese or {{pmin|South Korea|Korean}} {{Shiny}} {{p|Raikou}}, {{p|Entei}}, and {{p|Suicune}} distributed locally in 2010 to 2011, a reference to the {{OBP|Legendary beasts|M13}} in the thirteenth movie. ===Origin=== {{main|Pokémon world in relation to the real world#In the movies|Pokémon world in relation to the real world → In the movies}} Crown City is modeled after various locations in {{wp|Belgium}} and the {{wp|Netherlands}}. Director [[Kunihiko Yuyama]] {{wp|Location scouting|scouted}} {{wp|Brussels}}Behind-the-Scenes Report (Chapter 4: A Stroll in Brussels) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20100210204756/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/rokehan/04.html archived]) (Japanese), {{wp|Bruges}}Behind-the-Scenes Report (Chapter 7: The City of Bruges) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20100210204714/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/rokehan/07.html archived]) (Japanese), {{wp|Kinderdijk}}Behind-the-Scenes Report (Chapter 11: Windmills in Netherlands!) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20100210204807/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/rokehan/11.html archived]) (Japanese), {{wp|Delft}}Behind-the-Scenes Report (Chapter 12: Delft) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20100210204729/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/rokehan/12.html archived]) (Japanese), {{wp|Monnickendam}}Behind-the-Scenes Report (Chapter 13: A Small Port City) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20100210204811/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/rokehan/13.html archived]) (Japanese), and {{wp|Amsterdam}}Behind-the-Scenes Report (Chapter 15: Amsterdam) on the Pokémon movie website ([https://web.archive.org/web/20100210204734/http://www.pokemon-movie.jp/rokehan/15.html archived]) (Japanese) in search of towns and bridges covered in greenery. The combination of traditional and contemporary architecture in Crown City parallels the diverse range of architecture found in the cityscape of Brussels and Amsterdam. The city also feature canals flowing through it, alluding to both Amsterdam and Bruges being referred to as the "{{wp|Venice of the North}}" with historic system of waterways dating back centuries. The historic city center of Bruges is also registered as a UNESCO World Heritage Site with the medieval bell tower of the {{wp|Belfry of Bruges}} being its most prominent landmark. It also takes inspiration from the historical buildings and canals seen in Delft, where the city is also the birthplace of Dutch painter {{wp|Johannes Vermeer}} and a major production center of {{wp|Delftware}}. The windmills seen throughout the film alludes to {{wp|List of windmills in the Netherlands|windmills}} being an iconic symbol of Dutch culture with the {{wp|Kinderdijk windmills|group of 19 windmills}} in Kinderdijk being one of sites visited by the film director.
